prompt: Call the middle-school science fair finals like WrestleMania. The volcano kid is defending champion.
response:
WELCOME, LADIES AND GENTLEMEN, TEACHERS, PARENTS, AND STUDENTS WATCHING FROM THE BLEACHERS—

IT’S TIME FOR THE **MIDDLE-SCHOOL SCIENCE FAIR FINALS!**

Live from the cafegymatorium, under the fluorescent lights, with tri-fold boards standing tall like steel cages, we are moments away from the biggest showdown in sixth-through-eighth-grade academic entertainment!

And here he comes—

THE DEFENDING CHAMPION!

The Sultan of Sodium Bicarbonate!  
The Viceroy of Vinegar!  
The Erupting Emperor himself—

**“VOLCANO KID” JASON MARTINEZ!**

Listen to this crowd! He’s walking in with the safety goggles on, the lab apron flowing like a championship robe, and tucked under one arm is that papier-mâché mountain that took home first prize last year in absolutely dominant fashion!

But wait—standing across the aisle is the challenger!

She’s got data tables. She’s got laminated graphs. She’s got a hypothesis so clean it might need to wear gloves.

It’s **MAYA “THE VARIABLE” CHEN**, and her project on “Which Music Helps Plants Grow Best?” has been turning heads all afternoon. Her basil plants are tall, her control group is tight, and the judges have been circling her display like they know a main event when they see one.

The bell rings!

Volcano Kid starts strong—classic technique! He pours the vinegar into the crater, adds the baking soda, and HERE WE GO—

ERUPTION! ERUPTION! ERUPTION!

Red foam is cascading down the sides! The crowd is on its feet! A third-grader in the front row just yelled, “DO IT AGAIN!” That is championship presence right there!

But Maya isn’t rattled. She points calmly to her bar graph. She explains her independent and dependent variables. She’s got weekly measurements, repeated trials, and—OH MY GOODNESS—she’s citing a source from a university extension website!

The judges are stunned!

Volcano Kid reaches for the secret weapon—food coloring and dish soap! The eruption is bigger this time! Bigger! Frothier! More theatrical! He’s shaking the table slightly for dramatic effect, which may violate fair safety guidelines, but the people love it!

Maya counters with the scientific method! Question, research, hypothesis, experiment, conclusion—textbook execution! She’s not here to make noise. She’s here to win points on the rubric.

The judges confer.

Volcano Kid holds the blue ribbon high, daring anyone to take it.

Maya adjusts her poster board.

The room goes silent.

And the winner of the Middle-School Science Fair Finals is—

WAIT A MINUTE!

From the back of the room—

Is that…?

It’s **ELI “THE CIRCUIT BREAKER” THOMPSON** with a homemade lemon battery powering an LED!

He wasn’t even in the finals! He’s cashing in his extra-credit wildcard!

The judges are losing control! The principal is checking the rule sheet! The science teacher has both hands on her head!

This science fair has gone completely off the rails!

Ladies and gentlemen, we may not know who’s walking out champion tonight—

But one thing is certain:

In this gymnasium, on this afternoon, with 200 parents filming vertically on their phones…

**SCIENCE IS THE REAL MAIN EVENT!**
